Fortunately, the technical work on my latest book and spiritual child, "Narratives of Suffering and War," is nearing completion. I hope it will be published in the first half of Mehr and made available to those interested. Passages from the book's introduction are as follows: "Over the past fifteen months, tremendous and strange events have befallen this land and nation; events the likes of even one of which many people living in Europe, Australia, and North America do not experience in their lifetime. Two devastating wars that began with the blatant aggression of Israel and America against our country's soil, and whose aftershocks are still ongoing and have severely affected the security and livelihood of millions of Iranians. Tragically, more than four thousand of my and your compatriots have been drenched in their own blood during these two wars, including the innocent elementary school students of the 'Shajarat Tayyebah' school in Minab County. In addition, the horrific events that occurred after last Dey's protests and in the interval between the two wars, which took the lives of more than three thousand protesting and desperate citizens and cast their lifeless bodies upon the soil. In the midst of this, many families were bereaved, distraught, and destroyed, and they still remain in shock, mourning, and sorrow. Tragically, the ongoing sorrowful tale of the executions of Dey's protesters has added to the volume of these calamities. The psyche of many citizens has been wounded and afflicted during this period, and their wounds still bleed. The storm of events has made the atmosphere extremely dusty, and many people, with an abundance of fear and worry, are monitoring news filled with ambiguity, hoping that through the thought, judgment, and prudence of a few of the rulers, they might 'tunnel toward the light' and imagine a better future. The writer of these lines, although by the decree of fate has resided in North America for years and spends days and nights in this geographical region; yet his heart and soul are deeply bound to that soil and water and beat with longing for its prosperity and elevation, for 'my lamp burns in this house, my water is drunk from the jug of this Ayaz, and my bread is on this table'... Now that the waters have somewhat settled and the dust has subsided, I give thanks to the soul of the world that in those days when 'stones were raining down from the catapult of the heavens' and a heavy atmosphere prevailed, especially outside the country, and openly opposing the war was not an easy task; I did not become captive to the 'dictatorship of the atmosphere' and was not subjugated by the praise and blame of Amr and Zayd, I did not deviate from my national and ethical principles, and I defended the territorial integrity of Iran and the soil and water and my country. Despite all the minor and major criticisms I have had and continue to have regarding the country's mode of political governance...👇👇👇 https://www.instagram.com/p/DdZy_pMKrMh/?stkn=MTVpcWk3MXduMTU3bw==

"Never shall your image depart from the tablet of my heart and soul,
Never shall that graceful cypress depart from my memory.
Whatever burden of grief for you rests upon my wretched heart,
It may depart from my heart, but that one shall never depart from my heart."

On the arrival of the fourth anniversary of the passing of the dear Mahsa Amini and all those killed in the progressive and blessed movement "Woman, Life, Freedom" — a movement that, though suppressed, had lasting achievements and imposed itself upon the rulers, forcing them to accept the colorful lifestyles of citizens....

The written account and the collection of my writings during the days of the "Mahsa Movement" have been recorded in a chapter of the book "The Untrodden Path: Essays on Politics, Religion, and Society," read to the ear of history, and placed before audiences and those interested. In hope of the arrival of a bright tomorrow — a tomorrow in which economic and psychological security, freedom, social justice, and fundamental citizenship rights are institutionalized in our beloved country, and our sorrowful and suffering people no longer pass their nights and days and "still" in longing to obtain and taste them:

"Someday we will find our doves again
And kindness will take the hand of beauty
A day when the least song
Is a kiss
And every human being
For every human being
Is a brother...
A day when you come, when you come forever
And kindness becomes one with beauty
A day when we again scatter seeds for our doves, and I await that day
Even a day when I no longer exist"

Source: @Soroushdabbagh_Official

Execution, suicide, and the tormented psyche of society; the costs of securitized governance
Soroush Dabbagh - Yesterday, hearing three consecutive pieces of news, I became deeply bitter, and for moments the sky of my eyes turned rainy and tears overwhelmed me. Aida Heidari, the fiancée of Abolfazl Soleimani, one of those who lost their lives in the January protests, ended her life a few days ago. According to the families, Aida and Abolfazl were supposed to marry this very month. Also, Danial Karimi, the father of Amir Mohammad Karimi, one of those who lost their lives in the January protests, ended his life a few days ago. Amir Mohammad Karimi was an athlete and former member of Iran's national youth taekwondo team. In addition, Erfan Mirzaei, a twenty-one-year-old young rapper and singer, and one of those detained during the January protests last year, was executed in Isfahan a few days ago.
Over the past fifteen months, our beloved country has been embroiled in three devastating wars, numerous infrastructures have been destroyed, and several thousand innocent compatriots have been bathed in their own blood. For some time now, a naval siege has been added to the sanctions, placing additional economic pressure on the shoulders of citizens, to the extent that managing daily expenses for millions of Iranians has, according to official statistics published within the country, clearly become an exhausting and distressing ordeal. Moreover, in the January protests last year, several thousand protesting, desperate, and helpless compatriots fell to the ground, bathed in blood, and surrendered their souls to the Creator of life.
Truly, these are strange times. These days, I think a great deal about the dusty and ambiguous tomorrow of our society and country; a stricken society that has endured numerous individual and collective traumas over these same fifteen months...

Source: @Soroushdabbagh_Official

🔻Summer Velvet Whispers✔️ Soroush Dabagh's "Velvet Whispers" takes shape in continuation of a path the author has pursued for years at the intersection of philosophy, literature, mysticism, and lived experience; a path also followed in his earlier writings on DinOnline with reflections on prayer, solitude, suffering, death-awareness, and "existential wayfaring." Now, in "Summer Velvet Whispers," Dabagh returns once more to his solitude and places five new "whispers" before the reader: reflections on kindness toward oneself and "self-compassion," psychological shame and existential shame, the relationship between everyday language and poetic language, the connection between philosophy and poetry, and finally, the human longing for immortality. These writings, more than a collection of theoretical discussions, narrate the continuation of an inner dialogue; a dialogue in which philosophical and psychological concepts intermingle with poetry and literature to showcase the lived experience of contemporary humans and their relationship with self, others, and existence. In this new section, Dabagh still speaks of "horizontal wayfaring"; of a path that begins with the self, extends through solitude and reflection, and may ultimately lead to "arriving at oneself." 📎 Link to the full text of this note on the DinOnline website https://www.dinonline.com/46340/ 🆔 @dinonline

.Yesterday, the fortieth-day ceremony for my dear uncle, who has passed away, was held in Tehran. I am deeply grateful to all the friends and loved ones who, out of kindness, grace, and affection, offered their condolences over the past forty days. Despite my wish, unfortunately I was unable to respond to each and every one of the many condolence messages I received through Instagram, Telegram, WhatsApp, Clubhouse, and email. I take this opportunity to sincerely thank all those who have remembered me and my family during this time. What strange times these are, dear ones! The hand of fate denied me the chance to attend my uncle's funeral, burial, memorial, and fortieth-day ceremony.... I pray from the bottom of my heart for greater resilience for my dear compatriots in facing all kinds of adversities, bitterness, and unfavorable winds that blow in these turbulent times in our beloved Iran. I would like to treat the audience to some profound verses from one of the exquisite ghazals of the wise, contemplative Shirazi poet: The outcome of the workshop of existence and time is nothing but this— Bring wine, for the means of the world are nothing but this. In the few days you have respite in this stage, Rest well, for time is nothing but this. O ascetic, do not feel secure from the play of jealousy, beware— For the path from the monastery to the tavern is nothing but this. Hafez's name received a good seal, but in the eyes of the libertines, the account of profit and loss is nothing but this. https://www.instagram.com/p/Dc6STvmxaft/?igsi=bGpndjA5MmgzN2w=
